next.name: Starship | Starlink Group 31-2 (Starship Flight 15)
next.mission_description:
15th test flight of the two-stage Starship launch vehicle and 4th flight of Starship V3. Second Starship flight to deploy satellites (a group of Starlink satellites known as Starlink Group 31-2) into stable Low Earth Orbit and first ever to attempt returning the Starship 2nd stage back to the launch site.

The ship is expected to fly at an altitude approximately 275 km above Earth and complete approximately 14 orbits around the planet for more than 22 hours, with the ship expected to attempt returning back to Starbase, Texas on its launch pad by pad arms catching.

The booster’s primary test objective on Flight 15 will be executing a successful launch, ascent, stage separation, boostback burn, and landing by pad arms catching. This will also be the 1st Starship V3 booster to attempt returning to its launch site.

Starship will deliver 26 Starlink V3 satellites to orbit for the second time, which aim to greatly expand the network's capacity and user speeds. Each Starlink V3 satellite will add 1 Tbps of capacity to the constellation. 3 of the satellites have been modified with a suite of cameras to scan Starship’s heatshield and transmit imagery down to operators.

starship.note: Starship integrated flight-test record. Curated entries are the operator's; scripts/fetch_spacex_launches.py appends any flown Starship flight the launch record holds and this list lacks ("source": "launch_record"), so the tracker never ends behind the launch record again. Outcomes: success / partial / failure.

flights.milestone: First integrated flight. Cleared the pad; multiple engines out; lost in flight termination at ~T+4 min.
First successful hot-staging separation; both stages reached space before being lost.
Reached orbital-insertion velocity; first propellant transfer demo; ship lost on reentry.
Booster soft splashdown in the Gulf; ship survived peak reentry heating and splashed down.
First-ever 'Mechazilla' tower catch of the returning Super Heavy booster.
Ship splashdown in the Indian Ocean; in-space Raptor relight; booster catch waved off to a water landing.
Block 2 ship debut; booster caught at the tower; ship lost over the Caribbean.
Second booster tower catch; upper stage lost again early in the burn.
First flight of a reflown Super Heavy booster; ship reached space but lost attitude control before splashdown.
First clean Block 2 flight: Ship deployed eight Starlink simulators, relit a Raptor in space and made a controlled splashdown in the Indian Ocean; the booster flew its landing burn to the Gulf.
Last flight of the V2 vehicles: a reflown booster tested its landing burn over the Gulf, and Ship deployed simulators, relit a Raptor and banked into an on-target Indian Ocean splashdown.
First Starship V3: the booster's boostback burn failed and it was lost in the Gulf; Ship deployed 22 satellites, survived a Mach 7 flap test and splashed down on target.
Ship deployed 20 real Starlink V3 satellites and splashed down intact, still floating, in the Indian Ocean; the booster lit only 8 of 13 landing engines and hit the Gulf hard.
First flight to reach orbit: Ship released 26 Starlink V3 satellites, then an engine problem cut the planned six-orbit mission to about three hours; it splashed down in the North Pacific.

annual_launches.note: SpaceX orbital launch totals by year (Falcon 9 + Falcon Heavy + Starship orbital attempts). Finished years are curated; the current year is recounted from the launch record each run and flagged ytd (scripts/fetch_spacex_launches.py merge_annual_launches).
